newsitem.title: USA: Sony's TriStar chief Cooper resigns.
newsitem.headline: Sony's TriStar chief Cooper resigns.

text.p: The president of Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures unit resigned Friday after less than one year at the film studio.
In a statement, Sony Pictures Entertainment said Robert Cooper's duties will be assumed by Lucy Fisher and Gareth Wigan, both vice chairmen of Sony's Columbia TriStar Motion Picture Group.

According to people familar with his decision, Cooper, who was hired by former Sony Pictures executives Mark Canton and Alan Levine, wanted more autonomy than current Sony Pictures chief John Calley was willing to give.
Calley, who was hired last year to turn Sony Pictures around, has pushed for a more collegial arrangement where a group of top executives are responsible for deciding which films will be made.
Cooper was not available to comment.
Cooper joined the Sony division in July 1996 from his position as president of HBO Pictures and HBO Worldwide Pictures. He had been there for five years.
At HBO for five years, he was responsible for award-winning movies such as 1993's "Barbarians at the Gate" and "And the Band Played On."
